This is why the debate is more nuanced than #drillbabydrill or #juststopoil.

We need #oilandgas because we NEED oil and gas! 

We need it for 75% of the energy demand here in the UK. And that is AFTER the UK has spent billions of pounds and more than three decades decarbonising our economy faster than any other developed country, reducing CO2 emissions by more than 50% in that time.

This Labour Government has taken a big step towards fixing decades of inequality in women’s healthcare. We’re making menopause part of routine NHS health checks and renewing the Women’s Health Strategy so women across the country finally get the care and respect they deserve.

Women represent more than half of the population, and between reproductive health, pregnancy and birth, and longer life expectancy, they are more likely to need medical care across their lifetime. But there’s a huge gender bias in medicine that means women’s symptoms often go under-recognised or misdiagnosed. Too many women have been ignored, dismissed or told to just get on with it. That ends now. 

If you’re between 40 and 74, your free NHS health check will soon include questions about menopause. That means nearly five million women will have access to better information, earlier support and proper treatment. It’s about time. Three-quarters of women experience symptoms that can last for years, yet many never get the help they need. By putting menopause front and centre, we’re and making sure women’s health is taken seriously.

Separately, as part of a wider package of investment to rebuild community pharmacies, the morning-after pill will soon be available for free from pharmacies across England. Right now, whether you can get it for free is a postcode lottery and requires visiting a GP or a sexual health clinic. Now women will be able to access this basic right at their local pharmacy. 

These changes are part of our wider mission to rebuild the NHS, bring more care into the community and make it work for everyone. We’ve already started cutting gynaecology waiting lists, introduced Jess’s Rule so GPs think again if they can’t find a diagnosis and committed to eliminating cervical cancer by 2040. It’s all part of a bigger plan to build an NHS fit for the future – one that listens, acts and delivers for everyone.

I met with Matt Scott‑Campbell from the Moors for the Future Partnership today to discuss the major new investment coming to our local peatlands, including the moors above Stalybridge, Mossley, and the areas overlooking Huddersfield Road.
 
Through their Moor Resilience 2030 programme, the Partnership has secured £25 million for peatland restoration across the Peak District and South Pennines to 2030, alongside green finance initiatives the Partnership is pioneering. This is a huge opportunity for our area.

Healthy peatland doesn’t just support wildlife, it also slows the flow of water off the hills, which can help reduce the risk of flooding and peatland fires for residents along Huddersfield Road and nearby communities. It improves water quality, stores carbon, and makes our moorland environment more resilient for the future.
 
Matt talked me through the restoration and monitoring work already under way, as well as habitat enhancement proposals under development with land managers for the moors above Stalybridge and Mossley - I’m keen to see this work on move forward so that people here can feel the full benefit.
 
Thank you to Matt for sharing the work going and I’m to the Moors for the Future Partnership for their long‑term commitment to protecting our moorland landscapes.

ttPFUq2mfW54VKAR7t.text:
Allister comments after meeting on oil prices

Jim Allister MP said:

“Today’s meeting with Government ministers on the issue of fuel prices was, regrettably, largely disappointing.

"While there was no shortage of sympathetic words, there was very little in the way of concrete action for households and businesses struggling with the continuing cost of energy.

"Ministers gave no indication that they are prepared to remove the 5% VAT on home heating oil, despite the fact that so many households across Northern Ireland rely on it as their primary source of heat. Nor was there any commitment to retain the 5p per litre fuel duty rebate, a measure which has at least offered motorists some modest relief in recent years.

“Instead, much of the discussion focused on possible future regulatory changes, particularly in relation to the non-regulated wholesale fuel sector. While that may be worthy of examination, it offers no immediate help to families who are facing very real pressure today from the cost of filling their car or heating their home.

“Another unresolved issue concerns support mechanisms. In England there is a Crisis and Resilience Fund available to assist households facing acute financial pressure. Yet ministers were unable to clarify the extent to which any Barnett consequential will flow to Northern Ireland as a result.

“Ultimately, that means it will fall to the Northern Ireland Executive to decide whether to establish a parallel scheme to support local households.

“Given the scale of the pressures facing people, today’s meeting should have delivered far more than sympathetic words. What is required now is practical action that will genuinely ease the burden of high fuel and energy costs on the people of Northern Ireland.”

The Government’s new Schools White Paper, ‘Every Child Achieving and Thriving’, sets out a clear, long‑term vision for transforming education. It’s a thoughtful, carefully phased plan to strengthen education over the next decade, built on staged reforms, legislative foundations, and multi‑year investment to ensure consistency and stability across the system. 

Children deserve more than a narrow focus on tests. Every student should have a reason to go to school – an activity which draws them in and encourages them to look forward to their day. That’s why the plan includes a world‑leading fully-digital curriculum, ready for first teaching in 2028, with strong foundations in reading, writing, maths, speaking and listening alongside a revitalised focus on arts, culture and creativity. This comes with extra support for children with SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities) as well as an enrichment entitlement giving every child access to activities like sport, outdoor adventures, creative arts, and civic engagement. 

The plan aims to raise achievement and halve the disadvantage gap for children born under this government. This will be achieved through better targeted support, with £8bn of disadvantage funding based on household income, so help goes exactly where it’s needed most. Furthermore, new progress measures will ensure that all children have their progress recognised and celebrated. 

The SEND element of this White Paper is one of the biggest changes in a generation, creating a system in which children get the right support earlier, closer to home, and without long battles for help. There will be legally backed Individual Support Plans for every child with SEND. National Inclusion Standards will ensure consistent, high‑quality support everywhere. My Week in Westminster

I began Monday by speaking in Parliament to highlight the desperate need for greater SEND provision in Rossendale. The video of this is available on my Facebook page.

Later on, I attended a meeting of Red Wall Labour MPs, in which we discussed how to encourage Government and business investment into Northern towns. I'm glad to see we already have a lot of good things coming to our area, from the redevelopments in Bacup to improvements to the High Street in Rawtenstall, but I want to make sure our towns continue to stay a priority in the long-term. 

In the evening, we brought forward the Crime and Policing Bill, which will give the police new powers to tackle anti-social behaviour, shoplifting and street crime head on. From new Respect Orders to getting rid of the red tape stopping police officers from seizing stolen goods and bikes used for ASB, this law will empower our police to finally crack down on disorder. 

On Tuesday morning I met with the Tourism Alliance, to discuss how we can go about boosting the tourism industry in Rossendale and Darwen. Destination Darwen is a great example of how we can draw in regional and national tourism to the benefit of local businesses and communities. I'm keen to continue working with them on this. 

Later in the day, I met with representatives from Ceramics UK, a body that represents the entire ceramics industry in the UK, which has some members locally. We had a good conversation about what the Government can be doing to help the industry thrive and expand, and I'll be taking that forward in conversations with Ministers. 

I started Wednesday morning with the weekly Mission Champions meeting, discussing with Ministers how we can continue to deliver on our priorities.

🅿️ ☕️ 🌳 🍰🅿️ Lake Meadows Parking - The Cafe in the Park 🅿️ 🫖 🌳 🥪🅿️ 

Cllr Phil Turner and I swung by Lakeview Palace Cafe for a coffee and a chat with Mike, the owners about how the new parking charges have affected his business.

Lake Meadows hosts so many facilities, the skate park and playgrounds, the fishing lake, Swimking Pool, bowls club and ‘Men’s Shed’. We all know how special Lake Meadows is and we absolutely should be encouraging people to visit their green spaces locally. 

Of course, the re-opened cafe has also been a part of that mix making it even more social – in fact, there’s many people that meet weekly in the café just to socialise.

That’s why it’s so disappointing, bizarre, verging on the vindictive that the Council is actively trying to put small businesses out of operation by killing off their footfall. This café only opened in February this year and now they are facing a massive challenge caused directly by the decision from Basildon Council. 

I could see the impact immediately when there were only half the normal staff plus Mark present. Sadly, the charges have put people off – something that customers were telling me. During our chat, everyone kept checking their watches and phones to ensure they didn’t overstay their parking! 

It’s very sad but not surprising to see these parking charges hammer a newly opened small business. We need to rally round our small business entrepreneurs and those they employ. Our council should be protecting our community spaces such as this fantastic café, so I’ll be making sure to step up my visits to help support Mike, and I hope the local community does too!

And as I said earlier, I’ll work alongside Phil, Cllr Andy Barnes, Cllr Andrew Schrader - Billericay East, Cllr Andy Baggott, Cllr Martyn Mordecai - Billericay East, Cllr Tony Hedley, Councillor Danny Lawrence - Billericay West, Cllr Kevin Blake and Cllr Richard Moore to get this perverse car park charging decision reversed. 

Best wishes,

Richard Hold

Mentors can have a transformational effect on your life, they certainly did on mine. 

Many people have a narrow view of what mentorship really means. They often picture a mentor as a high-flying businessperson who spares you five or ten minutes of their time, points you in the right direction, and that’s it. If you’re lucky, maybe they’ll give you a bit more.

But real mentorship is much deeper than that— they are all around you and touch your life in many ways, often without you even realizing it.

For example, you’re three times more likely to start a business if your parents have their own business. That’s not just coincidence—it’s because you grow up in an environment where risk-taking is encouraged and running your own business is seen as normal. That was true for me. My, first mentor, my dad encouraged all of us to go into business, and we all did. He showed us what was possible when you work for yourself.

My next mentor was John Waterhouse, my business partner. He had faith in me during a really tough time in my life. I’d lost my job and was working in a video shop, and yet he still believed I could be a good business partner. We set up our company together in 1992, and he taught me a huge amount about business.

Another key mentor for me was my sister, Glyn. Mentors like her open your eyes to what’s possible—not just in the world, but within yourself. She gave me the confidence to take our small business, which had just a handful of offices, and grow it into a national network of 200 locations. She saw potential in me before I saw it myself, and she was able to communicate that belief in a way that really stuck.

Finally, there’s Harry Hill—not the comedian, but the former CEO of Countrywide, the UK’s largest estate agency. I met him after the financial crash, when our business was in real trouble. A few years later, I persuaded him to join us as a non-executive director. He completely transformed our business. At the time, it might have been worth a few m

Sarah Champion celebrates Labour Government’s funding boost for public health services in Rotherham

Sarah Champion has welcomed an increase in funding for public health services in Rotherham, the total amounting to an impressive £19,420,372 for the year 2025-26. This is part of the biggest real-terms increase, which amounts to £200 million nationally, after nearly a decade of reduced spending under the Conservatives.
 
Labour is committed to improving health outcomes across the country and building healthier communities. Through these public health grants, local health services will be able to deliver prevention and intervention programmes that are tailored to their residents.

Sarah Champion, Member of Parliament for Rotherham said:
 
“I welcome this uplift in spending to improve health outcomes across Rotherham. For too long, prevention has not been funded and I’m glad that is now changing, as prevention really is better than cure.  

“This funding will help reduce health inequalities, relieve pressure on the NHS and hopefully prevent people falling into ill health.
 
“This investment into our health services will make a real change locally and I look forward to seeing its implementation.
 
“The uplift from £18,434,695 to £19,420,372 for Rotherham, equates to £71.16 per constituent and a 4.95% increase from the year before, a much-needed investment into the people of our town.”

Child Practice Review into Neil Foden 

The findings of the Child Practice Review into the paedophile Neil Foden are deeply distressing and they must result in change. My thoughts are with the children whose lives were devastated by their abuse at the hands of their headteacher.

It is devastating to learn of the string of failures that led to the murder of Sara Sharif. 

Once again, the Family Court System was at the heart of a series of decisions that led to a child's death.

It is unthinkable that Sara should have been placed in her father's custody given the serious concerns about abuse and violence that had been raised against him but, having worked on the family courts system over many years, I know that decisions like these are not uncommon.

Women's Aid have previously found multiple examples of children and women who have been murdered at the hands of known abusers following the children being placed in unsafe contact arrangements.

The recent changes to allow greater transparency and reporting are an important step forward and will no doubt immediately begin to expose even more changes that need to be made. 

In the meantime, the Government should set out how we intend to reform the courts, at the very least by removing automatic parental rights for men who have committed murder or violent sexual abuse, as so many brave survivors have called for and for children to be considered victims of any domestic abuse in their household, regardless of whether it is physically perpetrated on them. In Sara's case, her mother and sibling were physical victims, but she was doubtless a victim too.

🚨PROTECTING HERITAGE IN 
BERKSWELL🚨

I have written to the Head of Planning at Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council, to register my formal objection to the outline planning application on the land off Windmill Lane in Berkswell.

The current iteration of the planning application demonstrates complete disregard for the impact of the development on Berkswell Windmill and its surrounding area.

Berkswell Windmill is an iconic Grade II star listed heritage site, which perfectly encapsulates the architecture and industry that makes our region so special. As we celebrate its 200th anniversary in 2026, it must be our priority to ensure that this cherished site is protected from intrusive development projects.

Most crucially, the approval of this planning application would set a dangerous precedent for the erosion of Green Belt and sites of historical significance in the future. This cannot be allowed to happen.

A special note of thanks to our local Conservative councillors who work so hard to protect our heritage and our greenbelt. 

Read my letter of objection below 👇

Over the last few months, I've been working with Help For Heroes  and the Royal British Legion  to support their campaigns for military compensation and pensions to be disregarded (not taken into account) when it comes to benefits – to ensure our veterans receive the full support they deserve.

I have submitted written questions and pushed Ministers on this, whilst it is great that military compensation is now disregarded for Universal Credit, each local council has the power to decide how it treats veterans and local benefits  - creating an unfair postcode lottery of support for our heroes.

South Tyneside Council have made the decision to disregard military compensation and pensions, which will ensure veterans living in South Tyneside get the full amount of benefits possible.

I hope that Gateshead Council will follow suit and ensure our veterans are treated with the respect and support they deserve.

I have written to Gateshead Council about this and I have submitted a follow up question to Ministers to ask them to instruct all Local Authorities to disregard the compensation and pensions of veterans and will keep pushing until all veterans get access to all the benefits they deserve.

The shutters came down on Connswater one last time at 6pm. A place that has been much more to our local community than simply bricks, mortar and a large glass front. 

It has served as a community hub, a meeting spot, the place where so many popped in to do their weekly shop, cash their wages, find their first Saturday job, grabbed a coffee, furnished the house or just for a quiet stroll from store to store. 

As I dandered through the centre in the final hour, the atmosphere was of quiet reflection, with many others taking their final walk and reminiscing of the shops that use to be in the various units on either side of the mall. 

A reminder of how much our communities change but on this occasion, a sad one. 

I joined Jonathan McAlpin from East Belfast Enterprise on the BBC’s Evening Extra with Mark Simpson this evening as we approached closing time - proudly wearing my most colourful odd socks for World Down Syndrome Day! A small but joyful act of celebration on a day otherwise tinged with sadness.

I welcome measures in today's Autumn Budget that bring help to our city. 

A higher minimum wage, ending the two‑child cap in Universal Credit, and freezes on rail fares and prescriptions ease pressure where wages are low and rents take nearly 40 percent of income. Money for school libraries and playgrounds matters in communities where child poverty is at 40 percent. Lower business rates for hospitality and leisure from next April support jobs and high streets.

On climate it is one step forward with charging investment, with hundreds of new chargepoints expected in Norwich, but two steps back with the scrapping of the ECO scheme, which makes fuel poverty and insulation problems harder to resolve.

Starting and running a business in 2025 Britain - let’s walk through it.

You’ve got a good idea, managed to save a few quid to invest and want to give it a go. Let’s say it’s a cafe. 

Generate wealth, create jobs and contribute to your local economy. Great idea. You just picked the wrong country to do it in.

Registering the damn thing is complicated enough, and that’s the easy bit. Next up is the bank account? You’re treated like a criminal and it takes week - opening a cafe, not a terrorist cell.

You manage to find a premise, good location. Oh, it costs a fortune. Rent through the roof and you’re forced to pay thousands to the council. For what? The filthy high street? The rapid customer service? Hmm. Yet another rip off. Inspections are a nightmare, it’s never-ending bureaucracy from people who have never created anything in their lives.

But somehow you get it off the ground and things go well. You need to expand, hire someone.

Ouch. PAYE, national insurance, pensions, HR policies, health and safety risk assessments. One wrong step and you’re facing an employment tribunal. Is it even worth the risk?

It’s becoming more and more expensive, and risky, to hire people? Why bother?

Maybe you try and get independent contracted help. Ah. IR35 puts a stop to that. We wouldn’t want any flexibility now, would we? That would make too much sense.

Your accountants already cost an absolute fortune. They’re bleeding you dry just so you comply with the layers and layers of regulations.

But let’s say it’s gone well, and your hard work is paying off. Turnover hits £90k. The dreaded VAT threshold. 

That means if you essentially then have to start charging VAT. That means everything gets 20% more expensive for your customers. Or you are forced to absorb the costs. Or you deliberately make less money to stay below the threshold. Just brilliant.

Maybe you want to keep the cafe open later? Serve some alcohol? Have some music on?

More licences. More costs. More inspections. M

I want to share something genuinely uplifting that I saw in Norwich the other weekend.

Jade Hunter, the headteacher at West Earlham Infant and Nursery School, told me about an extraordinary act of kindness led by two people, Annie Jennings and Lewis Wardale.

In the weeks before Christmas, Annie and Lewis decided to raise money to support children at the school. Donations began to come in, and it soon became clear their efforts could go further than they first planned. What started as help for a few children became support for the whole school.

Lewis ran 80 km, and Annie cycled 300km. Between them, they raised around £7,000, thanks to generous public contributions.

That support has now become Christmas hampers filled with gifts and toys for every child at the school.

For many families, especially those on fixed incomes, Christmas can be stressful and expensive. These hampers have lifted a real weight from parents’ shoulders. As Jade said, “Every parent wants their child to have a magical Christmas, and this has helped make that possible.”

When I arrived to help pack the hampers, the room was full of Annie and Lewis's friends and family, along with school staff. What could have felt overwhelming turned into something special. A proper community effort.

It shows what people can achieve when they look out for one another. Thank you to everyone involved. This is the very best of Norwich.

𝑾𝒆 𝒘𝒊𝒍𝒍 𝒓𝒆𝒎𝒆𝒎𝒃𝒆𝒓 - This morning, I had the real privilege of attending a service in Lurgan, where a new memorial was unveiled to honour Field Marshal Sir John Greer Dill, a true legend born in Lurgan on Christmas Day 1881. 

Dill’s roots in Lurgan ran deep—his father managed the local Ulster Bank, and his family had longstanding ties to the region’s linen and Presbyterian traditions. Over the course of his distinguished career, Dill would go on to play a pivotal role in World War II.

As Chief of the Imperial General Staff, he led British forces through some of the war’s darkest days. Later, he was sent to Washington, D.C., where his diplomatic skill and integrity established the "Special Relationship" between the UK and USA. His close partnership with US General George Marshall built a vital bridge between the Allies, uniting them in purpose.

Today was a fitting day to remember Dill, as it marked the 80th anniversary of his passing. It was a pleasure to meet members of the Dill family, who had travelled to be part of this commemoration. Field Marshal Dill’s legacy continues to inspire, and he is one of only two soldiers at Arlington National Cemetery to be honoured with an equestrian statue—a rare tribute to a Lurgan-born legend.

A heartfelt thanks to the RBL Lurgan and Brownlow Branch and ABC Council for their efforts in making this lasting tribute possible.

Lest we forget!

The EU will want another ‘multi-year’ agreement through which they catch more fish in UK waters than they do in their own. Elspeth Macdonald:

“Wild capture fisheries in our EEZ are naturally renewable – they don’t need chemicals and fertilisers to secure our food security – just skilled, knowledgeable and experienced fishermen who have dedicated their working lives to harvesting these resources efficiently and sustainably.
 
“Giving up rights to decide who fishes in our EEZ, and when and how, would be a betrayal of UK sovereignty. We don’t give the EU access to the UK EEZ to build windfarms or extract oil and gas, so why would we give away our hugely valuable fisheries resources?

“In addition, the UK must not allow itself to be threatened by the EU on market access. No other fisheries agreement in the north-east Atlantic couples access to fisheries with access to markets, and the UK Government must resist this strongly.”

On Sunday I stood with our community in remembrance of the seven Czech and Slovak soldiers that lost their lives in completing Operation Anthropoid, the mission to assassinate one of Hitler’s most senior officers, Reinhard Heydrich.

Heydrich was the then Nazi Governor of a large part of Czechoslovakia and the principal architect of the Holocaust.

They carried out their ambush on his staff car on May 27th and, as a result of their attack, which took place in the outskirts of Prague, Heydrich suffered fatal injuries and died on June 4th 1942.

Based in Leamington during the war, the soldiers were part of the several thousand strong Free Czechoslovak Army quartered here and their mission was supported by the RAF with training from the Special Operations Executive.  

Following the attack, the seven went into hiding to avoid capture before their location was betrayed. Despite their extraordinary bravery, they ultimately died in the crypt of a Prague church after a brutal firefight fought by 700 Nazi soldiers. The Nazis then sought retribution by razing several villages and the mass killing of their inhabitants.

Their courageous action and sacrifice is commemorated in the simple but powerful sculpture of a parachute in the heart of Jephson Gardens.

The Slovak Ambassador and senior staff from the Czech embassy were in attendance for what is always a most moving event, made more so by the singing of their respective national anthems by local children - themselves of Slovak and Czech heritage.

Our veterans are being treated “worse than terrorists”. That damning indictment is not from me as Leader of the Opposition, but from Labour’s own Northern Ireland Veterans Commissioner, David Johnstone.
 
Mr Johnstone is describing the Government’s Northern Ireland Troubles Bill, currently being pushed through Parliament by the Prime Minister. At a stroke, it will override Conservative legislation intended to protect our veterans from vexatious, historic claims.
 
Keir Starmer’s Labour Party are so slavishly devoted to the most contentious and damaging interpretation of the European Convention on Human Rights that they are pursuing a bill that their own adviser says is “eating at the very fabric of the Armed Forces”.
 
The Government’s approach means reopening decades-old cases where the only people left with records are soldiers who followed lawful orders, while IRA terrorists walk free because the weapons they used were decommissioned without forensic testing. Funnily enough, the terrorists tended not to keep scrupulous records.
 
Families, Johnstone said, are being given false hope of justice that will almost certainly never come. Instead, elderly veterans will once again be in the dock, dragged through years of legal warfare. That will be a national disgrace.

Statement on the introduction of the EU General Product Safety Regulations in Northern Ireland 

Jim Allister said:
 
"I am deeply concerned about the introduction of the EU General Product Safety Regulations 2023 in Northern Ireland from today, Friday 13th December.  This is a far-reaching law that, because of the Northern Ireland Protocol, the people of Northern Ireland did not make and cannot change. It demonstrates the practical folly of subjecting oneself to a foreign Parliament. 

"Like all legislation imposed in this way, the Regulation testifies to the fact that Northern Ireland has effectively been made a colony of an imperial power, but worse than this, its practical effect is to divide us from the rest of our own country which is not subject to this legislation. 

"Northern Ireland is a small part of the United Kingdom economy, and, fully integrated with it. Businesses depend on inputs from companies in the rest of our home economy based in England, Wales and Scotland. The burdens that this GPSR legislation places on people in GB seeking to sell products to Northern Ireland are such that in one sector alone, crafts, I am aware of eleven different GB companies that have chosen to cease servicing Northern Ireland from today, because the customs burdens are too severe.

"Contrary to the repeated line of the Government whenever, since July, I have raised this matter, this is having a devastating effect on small businesses. The only solution to this problem is to find a practical solution which first and foremost protects the integrity of the UK internal market and avoids distortion of the EU single market for goods.

"Happily, there is a solution to this problem which came from the EU, Mutual Enforcement, and which is set out in my EU (Withdrawal Arrangements) Bill."

I try to do it most years, I think I skipped the year I had a broken shoulder, and the route sometimes varies a little, but it is now a familiar journey for me at the end of September.  I am still feeling the after effects and some pretty sore legs and feet.  I suspect I will be back to the Foot Clinic in Tee Court before very long.

I also had the opportunity to visit the new Mind Garden at Leckford which is a collaboration between the John Lewis Partnership and Andover Mind.  The garden has been designed and developed with well being and sustainability in mind.  There is a real focus on pollinator friendly plants, to keep them fed throughout the seasons, but that also means there is colour. The clover lawn was absolutely incredible, especially given the efforts many gardeners make to rid their lawns of the plant, but an entire lawn of it was a thing of beauty, and even at this stage of the year buzzing with insects.

A number of constituents have recently been in touch regarding the charity Young Lives V Cancer and I have been to visit Jean's House in Southampton which supports young cancer patients and their families. The atmosphere there was absolutely lovely, really welcoming and warm, and it provides such a boost to families who might otherwise really struggle to find accommodation close to the hospital when they need it.  I also met up with their representatives in Birmingham at the start of this week, to ascertain how I can help them in their efforts.

I did also squeeze in a quick trip to Edinburgh for the events to mark 25 years of the Scottish Parliament. I loved visiting Riverford last week with my fellow Lib Dem MP, @Martin Wrigley MP for Newton Abbot 
 
The visit was organised by the Better Business Act campaign, and it’s hard to think of a business that better epitomises the campaign’s aim of promoting purpose-led companies than Riverford.
 
Not only has Riverford been employee-owned since 2018, but, as Martin and I learnt last week, it is going above and beyond to boost its sustainability and biodiversity credentials, including by installing solar panels and planting trees to capture carbon and protect the soil.
 
A great example of the latter is its new agroforestry project, where nut trees are planted on a field that can no longer be ploughed due to soil erosion.
 
The Better Business Act campaign is calling for social and environmental impacts to be aligned with shareholder returns in the job description for company directors.
 
It’s an interesting idea, and one that’s attracting a lot of interest, with over 3,000 businesses, including Virgin and Iceland, signed up.
 
With companies like Riverford proving you can do right by the planet and your profits, it’s little wonder the campaign is getting so much support.

Stalking is a deeply distressing crime, with victims subject to relentless and often debilitating abuse.

For far too long, victims have been subjected to the actions of stalkers who use any means necessary to intimidate, monitor and control them.

The Home Secretary is introducing groundbreaking measures, including new statutory ‘Right to Know’ guidance. This will give the police the power to identify online stalkers early, offering victims the protection they desperately need.

I am extremely proud that this specific change has been brought about thanks to the tireless campaigning of Blackpool woman Nicola Thorp, who was the victim of stalking for two years by a man online who set up almost 30 social media accounts to send her violent misogynistic messages.

Nicola is a shining example of how raising your voice and speaking out against misogyny can bring about real change and I’d like to thank her for her work on this important topic. 

Nicola said: "These new measures will empower victims to regain some much-needed control of their lives and police to bring abusers to justice."

The government has also announced that Stalking Protection Orders will also be strengthened and made more widely accessible. These orders can prohibit stalkers from approaching or contacting their victims and require them to attend programmes designed to tackle the root causes of their behaviour.

Courts will gain greater powers to impose restrictions on convicted offenders, even if no prior protection order was in place. This will prevent perpetrators from harassing their victims, including from prison, and courts will have the authority to apply protection orders against acquitted individuals if evidence indicates they remain a threat. 

These vital steps mark a significant shift in safeguarding victims and ensuring stalkers are held accountable for their actions.

If you need support, you can call the National Stalking Helpline on 0808 802 0300.

Airport Update

It was the last Friday before Christmas, and all through the house, not a creature was stirring – not even a mouse.

Yet, your Conservative Mayoral Candidate was hard at work, pouring over last quarter's Doncaster Council Finance and Performance Report. Unfortunately, there were only six lines dedicated to DSA. 

There has been plenty of social media chatter about the excitement of a plane landing there, but not much else to report.

And with Christmas upon us, I expect that the slow progress will slow down even further over the next couple of weeks.

So as there is little to report and this is the last airport post before Christmas, I thought I would share what I was hoping Santa would bring you and me.

My ideal Christmas gift would be for Oliver Coppard to return the £23 million he has taken from the people of Doncaster for his tram projects and then allocate £138 million of the £540 million awarded to South Yorkshire to help reopen our airport. He can then distribute the remaining funds fairly among each of our boroughs.

I’d also like to see Oliver and our Doncaster Mayor Ros Jones ask local MPs, such as Jo White, to lobby their councils for funding for our airport too. They often talk about their efforts to reopen the airport (although, as we know, the truth is they did nothing), and show up for photo opportunities, yet there is no evidence of them pushing for financial support from their councils. It's time for them to step up or shut up.

So, Ros Jones  and Oliver Coppard, I know you both must be wondering what to get me for Christmas 😂. So there you have it, and as you can see, it’s not just for me. In the true Christmas spirit, it is a present for all the good people of Doncaster. So let’s stop wasting Doncaster’s funds on Sheffield trams. Use taxpayer money responsibly and fairly to get our airport open.

If you agree with me then please do share this post.

Wishing everyone a Merry Christmas! Including our Two Mayors🎄🥂🎅

Best wishes Nick

Twenty years ago today four men detonated suicide bombs on the London Underground and a bus. Murdering 52 people and injuring nearly 800, many of whom still live with life changing injuries and of course the memories of surviving such atrocities.

London and the U.K. were not cowed by such cowardice shown by the terrorists. Londoners rose up as they always do and showed their grit, determination and their support and love for their fellow men and women. Our emergency services ran towards terror and showed such bravery. I was proud of the response from Westminster City Council setting up the family assistance centre.

I also remember poignantly the Victory in Europe celebrations that took part in central London three days later. I sat in St James’s Park with my one year old daughter and my parents in law who had grown up in Westminster during the Blitz and through the Second World War. We were surrounded by thousands of people on a beautiful sunny day. We were all determined to send a very clear message to those who wished to divide and terrify us - we stand united because light shines over darkness.

I’ve been working on amendments to the Crime and Policing Bill to better protect our children and keep them safer from child abusers. I have laid the following amendments which I hope the Government will adopt:

𝐖𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐞 𝐥𝐢𝐟𝐞 𝐨𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐝 𝐦𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫

It is shameful that the murder of a child is currently only subject to a whole life order in sentencing if it involves kidnap or sexual motivations.

My amendments to change the sentencing laws will make sure that any sick individual who commits this heinous crime should spend their whole life in prison regardless.

𝐑𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐯𝐚𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐬𝐞𝐱 𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬’ 𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐫𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭𝐬

In 2023 a mother spent over £30k going to court to terminate the parental rights of her child’s father – a convicted paedophile.

My amendment will automatically terminate the parental rights of convicted paedophiles for any children they have at the time of sentencing.

Children and families deserve the highest level of protection. My amendment will deliver that, ensuring paedophiles no longer have the power to make key decisions for their children and therefore continue to have power over the family.

𝐌𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐟𝐟 𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐝 𝐚𝐛𝐮𝐬𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐚𝐠𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐯𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐫

Residents with civil service pensions who are awaiting payments, following the problems experienced by Capita since taking over running the Scheme in December, may now be able to apply for hardship loans of up to £10,000. 
 
I have been contacted by a number of constituents who are facing issues and delays to the processing of their civil service pensions since December 2025 when Capita took over the administration of the scheme. 
 
The problems are being experienced across the country, with around 8000 people awaiting payments that are due and reports that the backlog of enquiries and reached 120,000 cases. Given the scale of the issue, members of the Scheme are also now having to deal with support lines being overwhelmed by the number of people trying to contact the company. 
 
It is shocking that so many people who should be able to rely on their pension payments have been let down and many are facing financial difficulties as a result. I am pleased therefore that emergency payments are now available. As the emergency payments are being processed as employer loans, pensioners are being directed to contact their former employer if their employment ended less than 12 months ago. 
 
Having contacted Capita on behalf of residents I have also been informed that they have put in place additional resource and that cases where there is a hardship element are being prioritised, focusing on death in service payments and those members who have retired but are not yet in receipt of pension payments.  

While the announcement of emergency payments is welcome, if you are affected by this issue and need assistance with escalating your own case, please do contact me at ben.spencer.mp@parliament.uk

🇬🇧🐑🌾 Thank you to our farmers.

To conclude British Food Fortnight, it was a huge privilege to attend the National Harvest Festival held at Westminster Abbey in the presence of Her Majesty The Queen.

In a service attended by 2,200 people, which included industry leaders, stakeholders, many farmers and growers, those in the food supply chain, school children and food charities, we all gave thanks to our farmers for all they do, throughout the year, in all weathers, to put great quality food on our plates. 

The service also focused on the fact there is still much to be done to ensure all within our communities still have enough to eat and don’t go hungry. 

As the lead organisation of the service, Love British Food led by Alexia Robinson have forged strong partnerships with food redistribution and food bank charities such as – Trussell, The Felix Project, the Coronation Food Project, and City Harvest – with volunteers joining in prayers for the relief of hunger and suffering. 

In recognition of this, the Bishop of Ramsbury gave a special address during the service, highlighting the importance of sharing and caring for those less fortunate.

It was a real disappointment that not one DEFRA Government Minister was able to attend such an important event. 

From the family farms that have been part of our countryside for generations to our young farmers bringing fresh ideas into the industry, British farming is the backbone of our rural economy - and needs to be fully supported. 

Over the last two weeks, we have seen communities right across the country to come together and celebrate all the hard work that goes into putting food on our tables every single day. There have been harvest festivals and services right across the United Kingdom, in many schools and churches, across many communities. 

It was therefore a real privilege to be part of the national service led by Her Majesty The Queen to conclude the special events. 

📷 Justin Tallis - Getty Images

Northumbria Police Miners' Strike Files Update

On Friday afternoon I met with senior representatives of Northumbria Police having written to them following the discovery that files relating to the policing of Orgreave and the Miners' Strike had been destroyed last year. We spoke frankly about the mistrust that this will have caused many in mining communities up and down the country, including those here in South East Northumberland and about the need for the investigation into the matter to be transparent.

The Police acknowledged this and expressed their professional embarrassment that these documents had been destroyed and assured me that an investigation had already begun to understand the decision making behind the actions. I look forward to further correspondence from them and in the meantime will continue to press the government for the inquiry into the policing of the full dispute that has been needed for so long.

Busiest time of the year for hospitality and the industry is SUFFERING.

The last two budgets, on top of an already immensely heavy tax burden. Skyrocketing rates. Insurance costs exploding. Energy costs soaring.

Hospitality runs on tight margins. It cannot absorb endless tax rises, stealth charges, and regulatory costs imposed by people who have earned a penny in the private sector. It will break. It is breaking. 

How can Reeves not understand it?

Someone running a pub will look at these numbers at just not hire the additional staff, not invest in the new beer garden, not refurbish the pub, not pour any money into the local economy.

It DRIES UP.

What's the point? When it's all just taken in tax? Why bother? 

So there aren't jobs for local youngsters, there aren't new contracts for redecorating firms, there is nothing. 

I just cannot fathom how those in Government don't understand this.

There is one answer. CUT TAX. Brutally cut tax. Everything else falls around that. One way, and that's to make the risk worth it. 

They want to grow the economy. We all do. But tax, tax, tax is not the way. It will never work. You need to give people INCENTIVES. 

And I don't mean back to pre-Labour levels - people forget how bad it has been for years. Slash it all back, in the most spectacular way. Make the gamble worth taking.

If they do expand the business, hire more staff, invest their capital? It has to be WORTH IT. The risk is big, but the possible reward must also be big.

ANYBODY who has run a small business understands this - it is so painfully obvious. 

Can you imagine how fantastically well the British economy would prosper in a low tax, low regulation environment? 

Instead we have this - a filthy tax swamp that is suffocating our rainmakers. 

Nothing will change until we get MPs, and civil servants, who have built businesses in the private sector.

In a week that sees a grim milestone in Ukraine I chatted to Ukrainian Action in Parliament yesterday. 

A charity set up here and in the US, they have coordinated an incredible 69
Convoys of aid into Ukraine since the war began. 

One of their most active local groups is the Devon group operating from Stoke Gabriel, who I met last year at the Dartmouth Food Festival. 

It was great to hear from Natasha Hartman and Phil Gardner how valued the Devon aid convoys are. 

On arrival in Ukraine they leave the trucks in Ukraine along with the aid, and travel home in trains and planes - so the Ukrainians can use the vehicles. 348 so far have been donated. 

Natasha told me someone recently drove all the way in a cherry picker, which is now being used in Zaporizhzhia. 

The charity also runs retreats for veterans and their families in the Carpathian Mountains, and thanks to donations of equipment they have taught disabled veterans to ski. The rehabilitation work with veterans and their families is likely to continue long into the future even if a peace deal is secured. 

Really inspiring work, and I look forward to catching up with the Stoke Gabriel crew again soon - and maybe even joining a convoy.

I had the pleasure of taking part in the Energy Research Accelerator roundtable, Next Generation Nuclear: Powering Britain’s Energy Future, in Portcullis House, Westminster.

It was a focused, question led discussion on how large reactors, SMRs, AMRs and fusion can strengthen the UK’s energy security, affordability and net zero pathway, alongside a renewables led grid. We also dug into the practical enablers that will decide whether we succeed: regulation that is fit for purpose, the skills pipeline, supply chain readiness, and public confidence.

These themes resonate strongly with my work at NEMO - Nuclear Energy Maritime Organization where we are focused on ensuring the right international frameworks are in place for nuclear applications at sea, and on bringing regulators and industry together early to reduce friction and accelerate safe deployment.

I am also proud to support this agenda through my role as a Board Director and Trustee of the Nuclear Institute - UK, championing the skills, professionalism and standards the UK needs to deliver at pace.

Thank you to Chris Moore for excellent chairing, and to Shawn Coles FCIM and the Green Infrastructure Week team for convening such a timely and constructive session.

It was also a pleasure to take part alongside Nick King, Trudy Harrison, Andrew Bowie, Mark Rouse, Zion Lights, Oliver Parsons, David Cole FREng, Abigail, Gary Jones, Claire Young, Tim Gregory, Amanda Baxendale, David Brinson, Tom Davis and many more.

That’s just a fact, however uncomfortable.

The number is utterly irrelevant - the principle is what matters.

Otherwise, what? Just because the task is too enormous, we don’t even try? These people are just allowed to stay, hanging around? It’s pure defeatism.

I believe that every single illegal migrant should be deported, along with any legal migrants who commit crime. If a legal migrant comes and breaks their visa conditions, then yes - they have to leave too.

Our hospitality and our generosity has been abused for too long. This is our country, this is our home. Visitors, legal or illegal, must play by our rules, or they should be forced to leave. Simple.

It feels like I’m smashing my head against a very robust wall, over and over. How is any of this controversial? Can anyone explain? I’m yet to hear a reasonable explanation.

Deportations don’t always mean raids. Stop paying them benefits, stop housing them, stop accommodating them. Pay them to go - hundreds of thousands will leave voluntarily. And those that don’t? Then yes, they must be securely detained and forcibly removed.

Will it happen overnight? No. Does it need to be our policy objective? Absolutely, yes.

They are here ILLEGALLY. There must be consequences to that, otherwise why bother with borders at all? If people know they can come, and they know they can stay - they will keep coming and coming and coming. OBVIOUSLY.

The Radio Teleswitch (RTS) Phase-Out is underway - the infrastructure that supports it has reached the end of its natural operational life and is being replaced by smart meters. 

RTS uses radio signals to instruct specific RTS electricity meters to switch between peak and off peak rates. These electricity meters were designed to support consumers who may use electric storage systems and panel or immersion heaters in water tanks, which typically charge and heat up at night. 

If you think you may have RTS equipment in your home or business, you should contact your energy supplier urgently, and they will arrange for it to be upgraded.  Energy suppliers are standing by to prioritise RTS meter upgrades and respond to any issues quickly.  I have been informed by Ofgem that a small number of my constituents still have not upgraded - please double check this isn't you!

I was honoured to deliver the 25th Bernie Grant Memorial Lecture earlier this week. Bernie Grant was one of Labour's first Black MPs, elected to office in 1987. He was a giant of British politics, a community champion, and one of the most principled voices ever to sit in Parliament.

But Bernie did not just make history; he changed it. His politics were rooted in the radical tradition of anti-colonial struggle. He was unapologetic about calling for reparations, not as a fringe demand, but as a necessary part of justice.

He changed history by challenging its telling. He reminded Britain of the truths it tried so desperately to forget—the truths about empire, about colonialism, about slavery, and about the lasting debts owed to African people and their descendants. 

This week, we paid tribute to a political visionary and renewed our commitment to continue his legacy, challenging colonial amnesia and demanding justice for the lasting damage of enslavement and colonisation.

Drive down almost any country road and you see the same thing. 

Litter lining the roads. Plastic caught in hedges. Fast food packaging scattered across the grass. Crisp packets fluttering in the wind. Rusting energy drink cans just laying about. What message are we sending to children as they watch the rubbish pile up? It’s disgusting.

Nobody talks about it. We’ve just accepted it as normal. It infuriates me.

There was a time in this country when this level of disrespect would have been unthinkable. People took pride in where they lived. There was a clear expectation that public spaces would be kept clean and orderly, and that those who did otherwise would face consequences.

This was not that long ago. The decline has rapidly accelerated. Britain is increasingly resembling a third world country, and I do not like it. Immigration from said cultures has evidently played a large part. I’ll get abused for saying it, but it’s true. We all know it.

Once we start accepting visible decline in the small things, it rarely stops there. It hasn’t stopped there. It will get worse and worse and worse. The filth will pile up.

Britain should not look like this. It is not unreasonable to expect clean streets, clear roadsides, and public spaces that people can take pride in. Is that too much to ask for? I think not.

A Restore Britain Government would not tolerate it. Proper enforcement of littering and fly-tipping laws. Visible consequences for those who degrade our countryside. Deportation for foreign fly-tippers. Investment in keeping streets, roads, and public areas clean. Compulsory litter picking for non-violent offenders and healthy benefit claimants who consistently refuse work.

Most importantly?

A cultural shift.

Britain does not have to be a dumping ground.

It doesn’t have to be like this. We will not accept it. We will change it.

We will set an example to our children and grandchildren.

There is now a political party that will clean up our country.

Restore Bri

In January, the Labour Party was under immense pressure to act on the rape gangs. After public uproar, they announced these local inquiries in order to quell that rage. In a way, it worked. The anger subsided, and the debate moved on. At the very least, there would be some minor investigations that may lead to something greater.

For them to announce, on the last day of Parliament before recess with barely any notice, that even this pathetic effort was to be binned? It’s low, even for the Labour Party.

Why have they done it? Primarily, they are petrified of the organised Muslim vote in a growing number of their constituencies - they don’t want to lose their seats to the pro-Gaza independents.

Sectarian politics is here to stay. It will grow and grow and grow. Demands for Pakistani airports will soon be the least of our concerns.

It's scary.

We have now raised over £525,000 in under two weeks for our inquiry into the rape gangs, a number growing every day. 

I invite MPs from all political parties to join our efforts.

Labour, Conservative, Reform, Lib Dem. This is not a party political issue. It's about good versus evil. I will work with anyone.

As has been well documented, I am an independent MP. I’m not doing this for votes in May, I’m doing it to hopefully assist in delivering some form of justice.

To ALL MPs - help us to shine a light on these horrors, because quite frankly, this inquiry is our only option now.

It’s time to scrap the Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) mandate. This little-known law bans future sales of petrol and diesel cars and is a well-meaning but ultimately destructive piece of legislation.
 
Shortly after becoming Business Secretary in 2023, I held meetings with many of the major car manufacturers in Britain. In public, they welcomed the drive to make vehicles electric (no one wanted to look like they were not on the green bandwagon). In private, however, they were very downbeat about demand for EVs, scathing about the pace of supporting infrastructure such as charging points, and very, very worried about their financial futures.
 
This was a flashing red warning light for the economy, and I made sure it was known across government. I didn’t believe the ZEV mandate was working, and I fought to scrap it. In doing so, I convinced then Prime Minister Rishi Sunak to at the very least push back the ban on petrol and diesel cars to 2035 from 2030.
 
In response, Labour attacked us for “selling out the biggest economic opportunity of the 21st century” and after entering government they shifted the deadline back to 2030. You only need to look at what’s happened since to see the sheer stupidity of their response.
 
As Business Secretary I oversaw a £100m investment in Stellantis’s car plant in Ellesmere Port. In February this year, under Labour, Stellantis confirmed the closing of their Luton factory, putting 1,100 jobs at risk. In September 2023, I was in Oxfordshire to welcome BMW’s £600m investment into its Oxford Mini plant. This year, under Labour, BMW announced that investment had been paused, citing “uncertainty”.
 
I could go on, but you get the picture. Under the Conservatives, the direction was clear: decarbonise, but do so in a way that keeps Britain competitive. That meant leaning into investment, listening to manufacturers, and being willing to adjust targets when the market and infrastructure were not keeping up.
 
What we are seeing now is the opposite

Like the Great War, soon the Second World War will be out of living memory. And as it fades, so too does our chance to hear the stories directly from those who lived through it.

Remembrance Sunday is about telling these stories. It’s about remembering the individual acts of courage and the sacrifices families made in defence of our country.

But the more time passes from these moments when Britain stood together, the more Remembrance Sunday serves another purpose.

We remember to remind us that we are part of something bigger than ourselves. That all of the comfort and freedom we now enjoy is thanks to people we never met, fighting and dying to defend a country they thought worth defending.

A nation is only a nation when people are prepared to defend it. And it is both tragic and concerning that many people in Britain today no longer feel that call.

Only 10 per cent of Britain’s 18- to 28-year-olds say they would fight for their country. And while it may be tempting to see this through the lens of entitlement – typical of a generation that doesn’t know how good they have it – I think it goes much deeper.

🇺🇦 𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐢𝐚𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐲 𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐨 𝐔𝐤𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐞

It was an honour to represent the UK Parliament on a cross-party delegation marking the fourth anniversary of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The UK Government signed a historic 100-year partnership agreement with Ukraine last year and has long been a steadfast ally and supporter of Ukraine and its people. Today, more than 150 Ukrainians live in Oldham as part of the Homes for Ukraine programme, with residents opening their hearts and homes to provide safe sanctuary.

Because the war has resulted in restricted airspace over Ukraine, access must be achieved through a neighbouring country. The delegation therefore travelled via Moldova, where it was a pleasure to meet the Ambassador and her team, as well as parliamentarians and the Speaker of the Parliament of Moldova.

The first leg of the visit was to the port city of Odesa, which has endured almost daily attacks on its infrastructure and residential areas. During our overnight stay, we were called to the bunker as an air raid siren sounded, quickly followed by drone and missile bombardment in the neighbourhood where we were staying. At dawn, reports confirmed that four residential blocks and a local school had been struck. It served as a stark reminder of how everyday life continues under the shadow of war.

We visited the nearby port area to hear about the impact of the war on exports, particularly given Ukraine’s critical role in the global food supply. We also visited the awe-inspiring Odesa Opera House, one of many magnificent buildings reflecting the country’s rich cultural heritage.

It took almost as long for HMS Dragon, a single fast ship to get to Cyprus, as for much of the Royal Navy to get to the Falklands...the other side of the world in 1982.

The Falklands (1982) – Margaret Thatcher as Prime Minister

On 2nd April 1982, the same day Argentina invaded, Thatcher’s cabinet officially approved the formation of a naval task force.

The core of the task force, including the aircraft carriers HMS Hermes and HMS Invincible, set sail from Portsmouth on 5 April 1982, just three days after the formal decision was made.

The task force travelled approximately 8,200 miles, reaching the exclusion zone around the islands by 30th April 1982, taking roughly 25 days to arrive at the conflict zone.

Cyprus (2026) – Keir Starmer as Prime Minister

Following a drone strike on the RAF Akrotiri base on 2nd March 2026, Starmer announced on 3 March 2026 that the Type 45 destroyer HMS Dragon (a single ship) would be sent to reinforce the region.

HMS Dragon DID NOT depart Portsmouth until 10th March 2026, exactly one week after the announcement. 

The ship arrived in the waters off Cyprus on 23rd March 2026. It took 20 days to be ready and travel the approximately 3,500-mile journey from the UK .

I understand that even my most ardent supporters may not share my view on this issue. Nevertheless, I ask you to read both the text below and the attached piece before drawing your own conclusions.

While focusing on local priorities, I became increasingly aware of a national crisis, one that affects men and boys across the country. That led me to devote significant time and energy to this issue, helping to produce four reports focused on the challenges they face.

Many sneered at my work. They laughed when I called for a Minister for Men and a Men’s Health Strategy.

But the sneering is starting to fade. A Men’s Health Strategy has now been introduced. And perhaps, just perhaps, a Minister for Men may one day follow.

One of the darkest facts I uncovered during that time still haunts me: 13 men a day were taking their own lives. That figure has now risen to 14. Fourteen men, every single day, feel so lost—so hopeless—that they believe suicide is the only way out.

Can we really call ourselves a civilised society when that is the reality?

Now, I know I may lose support for speaking out today. But I wasn’t in Parliament to win votes. I was there to serve, help, and protect my constituents.

I’m no longer in Parliament, but I still feel a duty to use my voice.

I sit in Parliament listening to these ministers, and it’s all just so depressing - the vast majority of them have never run a business, and it SHOWS. You would not believe how bad it is. 

They think ‘work’ means turning up to an office between 9 and 5, answering a few emails, and going home at the end of the day. Nice lunch break, few coffees away from the desk, probably a smoking break or several. It doesn’t - not for the millions of men and women who actually create the wealth that funds the state.

Running a small business isn’t a job. It’s a way of life. It is life. It’s 24/7/365. It’s relentless. You are the accountant, HR department, compliance officer, cleaner, marketer, and customer service team - all in one. There’s no sick pay, no safety net, and no taxpayer-funded pension waiting for you.

Holiday? Good luck. If you do manage to get away, it’s checking the phone all day, every day. Wife/husband obviously getting pissed off. We’ve all been there...

It’s all on you. Every invoice chased, every tax deadline met, every bit of red tape navigated is on you. And if you make one mistake, one error, one small slip-up, the state comes after you - in a relentlessly efficient manner that is never afforded to us when we ask questions of it.

Most MPs have no idea what that feels like. They just don’t. We’re going to see more of this in the budget I’m sure. More hurt. More pain. More tax. They don’t get it.

They don’t understand that when a small business owner gets hit with another tax, it’s not absorbed by a ‘budget’ - it’s taken straight out of their family’s pocket.

There is no ‘deficit’ in the business world - that’s called going bust.

And they certainly don’t understand what real risk looks like. Support systems matter, but they should never replace the fundamental role of a parent/guardian.

A British visa is a privilege, not a right. With that, comes responsibility and conditions. Or so it should.

Illegal immigration grabs the headlines, but this is more important. Just because somebody came legally once, does not mean that they should be able to stay forever.

Any visa granted should provide clear and sustained benefits to the British people - the needs of the migrant are entirely secondary to that. In short - if an individual is going to come to the UK, they should give more than they take. Their presence, immediately and over the long term, should not be a drain on our resources.

It should be dependent on the individual speaking proficient English.

It should be dependent on the individual financially supporting themselves and their family.

It should be dependent on the individual following our law, to the letter.

It should be dependent on the individual respecting Britain, and who we are.

I have no issue with cancelling work visas if that individual is not working, unable to speak English, living off the taxpayer. Is that not common sense? Any self-respecting country would.

Of course, legal immigration needs to be brutally slashed down. Far more people need to be leaving the country than entering, but ultra-high skilled immigration which benefits the British people in areas where we are lacking is welcome. If they come, work, integrate and belong - that is positive immigration.

A far-reaching review of existing visas is needed. Skilled visas for kebab and vape shops? No. Enough.

Bread update! 😊

Could let a month go by without a quick Bob's Bread. Two things.

✅I think I have sorted a reliable recipe: 500g of Wessex Mixed Grain (sold in Brighstone Store), 350ml of warm water with a big teaspoon of honey mixed in with the yeast sachet so it has a bit of time to come alive. Two tea spoons of sea salt which I crush by hand.

✅I have tried to cut corners with a one-rise bread, I don't think it works, so I give the mix a good knead and leave for at least 40 minutes, and then gently punch the air out and knead it for a minute or so, then put it in a bread tin.

✅I'm also putting a seed mix into the dough. I experimented with a mix from M&S - Good Gut mega mix - and it's good as a snack but didn't work in the bread dough, especially as the coriander seeds dominate.

✅Then stick in over for 35/40 minutes. This loaf is good for you, you know what is in it, and twice risen makes it taste good for a couple of days.

I've been trying to do this often enough so that it becomes habit. it now is, more or less. 😊 Which is good. 

Bob

Britain can’t spend what it doesn’t have. 

That’s why the two-child benefit cap matters. It’s about fairness, because families on benefits should face the same choices as working households about having children, and affordability, because scrapping the cap means higher taxes for everyone else. 

But Keir Starmer is preparing to give it up. Not because it helps children (the Institute for Fiscal Studies has found no evidence it does) but because over 100 Labour MPs are demanding it, and his rival Andy Burnham has branded it “abhorrent.” Starmer is too weak to say no. 

This will cost £3.5 billion a year. That money doesn’t appear out of thin air. It means higher taxes, more borrowing, and less money for schools and hospitals. All to keep his left-wing backbench MPs happy and his party together. 

This is part of a pattern. Labour has already blown a multi billion pound hole in the welfare budget by scrapping reforms and through a series of u turns. Every time Starmer faces pressure from the left, he pays them off with taxpayers’ money because he is too weak to do the right thing. 

Meanwhile, Reform, the Lib Dems, and the SNP all want to scrap the two child cap. A coalition of left-wing parties prepared to drive up welfare spending, ignoring the consequences for working families and future generations. 

Only the Conservatives are prepared to make the responsible choice. We introduced the cap in 2017, and if Labour scrap it, we’ll bring it back. Because fairness matters. Families across Britain budget carefully and live within their means. They expect their government to do the same.

Unemployment rising. What on earth could have caused that? Who could have possibly predicted it?! Oh. All of us.

This is not a mystery. It’s the inevitable result of a government that keeps taxing work and punishing the people who actually create jobs and generate wealth. 

OBVIOUSLY.

Treating business as a lemon to squeeze, not a tree to grow.

Employers’ National Insurance - an actual tax on employing people - has risen again and again. You tax employment, unemployment goes up. This is so painfully obvious. How can these useless gnomes not see it?!

Then there’s corporation tax - hiked as well. Business rates that crush high streets. VAT thresholds that trap small firms and discourage growth. Brutal dividend thresholds that mean earning more is often simply not worth it.

Every single one of these is a tax on productivity, a tax on success.

And when you tax something, you get less of it.

Ask any small business owner. They’ll all say the same.

The system DOES NOT work. I’ve built businesses, run businesses. One of the few MPs to do so… If more of us were in Westminster, we may actually get somewhere.

We now have a country where it’s easier and cheaper not to work than to employ or be employed. Easier to sit on your arse doing sod all than actually contributing. If you’re fit to work, you must work. It’s that simple.

You can’t build a vibrant economy on higher taxes, higher regulation, and higher energy costs.

You just can’t. Certainly not with Reeves in charge. She may be a pleasant woman, I don’t know, but she is utterly incompetent. Weak, inept, failing. She must go.

The Treasury’s addiction to taxation is killing the very people it relies on to fund the state.

What can we do to fix it?

- Cut Corporation Tax to the lowest in Europe - send a clear signal that Britain is open for business.
- Undercut our neighbours. Go for their business. Compete against the Europeans. Win.
- Abolish Business Rates entirely for small companies.
- Double the VAT threshold

There’s been too much doom in our politics of late. Too much fatalism about our future.

So, why then, am I bullish on Britain?

My confidence isn’t due to a lack of awareness or complacency about our present malaise. I see it, like so many it pains and motivates me.

The lack of real wage growth since 2008. The highest industrial energy costs in the world. The record high taxes, government spending, and debt interest payments. The two million more people on out-of-work benefits than five years ago. The 7 million on the NHS waiting list. Or one in five students actually earning less for having gone to university. That’s not to mention the record shoplifting and court backlogs, and the endemic, so-called ‘petty’ lawbreaking.

Our present malaise is explicable. In recent decades, those in charge have traded out the fair, decent and efficient instincts of the British people as the guiding force behind our policy for their own supposed ‘rationality.’  

All too often they disparaged public opinion as “populism”, choosing instead to work against the grain of sentiment of the British people. Our political and bureaucratic class would say one thing in public to placate the public, but do another in practice.

We’re confronted with manifestations of this madness on a daily basis. A foreign terrorist’s right to stay here trumps the public’s right to walk safe streets. We won’t drill in the North Sea, but we will import oil and gas from Norway – who drill from the exact same sea. We’ll trade a car made in Sunderland, for one made in China. We’re for free speech, but Islam should get its own blasphemy law. We must give-away the strategically important Chagos Islands to Mauritius to preserve our reputation at international law conferences. 

Those are the results of the so-called rationality of those in charge of our country. It’s a joke – and the joke is on us.

I was taken aback by the generous offer, but slightly wary of the idea, conscious that on a cold and wet Monday night in Nottinghamshire, we might not attract many people and it could backfire.

I had spent the previous few years attending Tory events where as few as a dozen people turn up. Happily, I was proven completely wrong.Reform sent out invites to members within a 30-mile radius and, at a few days’ notice, they brought together 1,500 people. The irony seems to have been lost on Mr Ratcliffe. Secondly, it was the misinformation Mr Ratcliffe was perpetuating; I would have thought a savvy businessman would have checked the evidence before making his claims. As ever, Nigel Farage has jumped on this bandwagon to add his divisive message. For clarity, the UK population has increased by roughly 2.7 million due to migration since 2020, rather than the 12 million he claimed, and net migration is now falling. My anger was that this is personal to me. My husband, John, is an immigrant. He came over from apartheid South Africa when he was 10. Yesterday, I was in Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, to mark 3 years since Russia launched its war. 

As the U.S. turns away from Ukraine, it was a privilege to stand with other world leaders as we gathered in the central Maidan Square to honour fallen soldiers and those who have lost their lives throughout this war. 

There were 16 UK parliamentarians on this trip, and to share this with so many Liberal Democrat colleagues, two of whom are former members of the serving military, was incredibly poignant. 

Leaders from across the world, including Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederriksen, Sweden's Prime Minister Ulff Kristersson and the Prime Minister of Spain, Pedro Sanchez, came together to join President Zelensky and stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine. 

As we waited for international political leaders to gather, it was extremely useful to hear his insights into the role of the British Armed Forces, following Putin's invasion and what could happen next. 

I know the people of Torbay are steadfast in their support for the people of Ukraine in their fight against Putin's illegal war.

During my few months of being an MP, this is the most important event I have  had the privilege of representing the Bay at. If we fail to stop Putin now then he will be back for more of our other sovereign states. 

As a representative of our communities in Torbay, it was incredibly moving to lay a candle from us here in Devon. 

Justin Trudeau was generous by attending this service to demonstrate his solidarity with the people of Ukraine. It was a pleasure to meet him. 

If only the U.S. president was in attendance...

John F. Kennedy once said:

"Let every nation know, whether it wishes us well or ill, that we shall pay any price, bear any burden, meet any hardship, support any friend, oppose any foe to assure the survival and the success of liberty."

We said goodbye to a very special person today at Hull Minster.

John Prescott was a staunch defender of working people and a proud trade unionist who will be remembered for his conviction, courage and strength of character.

He was instrumental in building the Labour Government that transformed the lives of millions across the nation and his legacy will live on well beyond his lifetime. 

The time he and I went to a conference in Mexico together will always stay with me. He had stories that were just out of this world. This was many years after he had ceased to be one of Hull’s MPs, but he still took time to seek out a foreign delegation to help with a bit of casework relating to a local ship that had been lost at sea many years ago. It was brilliant to see.

Despite reaching the very top - he is, in many ways, the model of how to be the UK’s Deputy Prime Minister - several of the eulogies referenced his personal sense of self-doubt and social shyness. I think any working class person who has succeeded in their chosen career will be able to relate to that. I think it meant people could also relate to him. His achievements were considerable and important. It was great to see the love and respect on display towards him today.

RIP Lord John Prescott, 1938 - 2024

Business Secretary Johnathan Reynolds has announced a new Business Growth Service launching in early 2025 allowing those in Blackpool and beyond to get quicker and easier help, support and advice. 

Small businesses consistently say that they find the business support landscape fragmented and complex, with only 26% of UK SME employers reporting in 2023 to have sought external advice or information in the last year. 

The Business Growth Service has been designed to address this, offering a sleek, UK-wide business support system with a revamped web offer. It will be developed and will work in partnership with small businesses, local and devolved governments across the UK, with locally led delivery at its core, to ensure the service provides the information and resources smaller firms need from government.   

Inspired by successful business support agencies internationally, the Business Growth Service will be an integral part of the Small Business Strategy that will be published in 2025.  

The average small business owner spends over 33 hours every month on internal business admin – valuable time which the government aims to decrease through the new streamlined service which will signpost small firms to practical help. 

This, alongside a other measures announced in the run up to Small Business Saturday, confirms the government's commitment to the nation's small firms and self-employed individuals who are vital to wealth creation and economic growth.  

Read my blog to see what Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds had to say about how these changes will impact small businesses: www.chriswebb.org/news/new-government-growth-service-to-save-small-business-time-and-money
